one_liner: Policy and coordination job in NOAA's Office of International Affairs: advise leaders, support negotiations and agreements with foreign governments, and plan international meetings and visits.
fit_summary: Daniel's policy knowledge, relationship-building, and government-client consulting at IEM line up with the External Awareness, Oral Communication, and Partnering competencies. The posting requires one year of specialized experience that includes all three international elements (partnerships and negotiations, foreign visits and travel planning, policy positions and briefings). Nothing on file shows international work, so Daniel qualifies only if the IEM role or other experience truly covered those tasks.
eligibility: Open to the public: this announcement lists public, federal-transition, and veteran hiring paths, and U.S. citizenship is required. A separate status-only announcement (UNSEC OIA-27-13098189-ST) exists, but Daniel cannot use it without federal status.

Positive education requirement for the 0131 series: a qualifying degree or 24 semester hours in fields such as political science, international relations, economics, or history. An alternative is four years of experience related to foreign affairs. Transcripts must be submitted.
One full year (52 weeks) of specialized experience at the GS-09/ZA-2 level that includes all three listed international elements, met by the closing date. Graduate education may substitute in part.
Must be able to obtain a Non-Critical Sensitive (Secret) clearance after a background investigation.
Selective Service registration if applicable; a one-year probationary period applies.
strategy: Before applying, confirm with yourself that you can honestly document all three specialized-experience elements. If IEM work involved international clients, foreign delegations, or international disaster cooperation, describe it explicitly; if not, this posting is likely out of reach.
Upload transcripts showing your political science or related coursework, since the positive education requirement is checked strictly. Add official course descriptions if course titles are unclear.

Frame IEM experience in the posting's language. For example, coordinating with government agency partners becomes 'inter-agency coordination,' and client deliverables become 'drafting reports and briefing materials for senior leadership.' Tie this to environmental or hazard policy where it is accurate.
Keep the resume to two pages. Give each job start and end dates (month/year) and hours per week, and put the three specialized-experience elements as clearly labeled bullets.

Preview the questionnaire at the provided link and answer 'expert' only where your resume supports it. Prepare for the Job Knowledge Test by reviewing NOAA's international programs and U.S. ocean, climate, and science diplomacy.
The window is short (Oct 26 to Nov 2, 2026), so have documents ready before it opens and submit early.
resume_bullets: Supported development of [partnership/agreement] with [foreign government or international organization], drafting [number] reports and negotiation support materials for [audience] ([dates], [hours]/week).
Planned logistics and agendas for [number] international meetings and foreign delegation visits, coordinating travel and briefings with [agencies/partners].
Drafted policy positions and briefing materials on [emergency management/environmental policy topic] for [senior client leadership], informing [decision or outcome you can verify].
interview_questions: Describe a time you helped prepare positions or materials for a negotiation or agreement. What was your role?
How would you brief NOAA senior leadership on a foreign policy development affecting a bilateral science partnership?
Tell us about coordinating a high-level visit or international meeting under tight timelines.
How do you build and maintain relationships with partners whose priorities differ from your agency's?
watch_outs: The specialized experience must include all three international elements, and domestic emergency-management consulting alone likely won't qualify.
The positive education requirement means a missing or unclear transcript leads to automatic disqualification.
The announcement is open only one week, and you must pass a Job Knowledge Test and a Secret clearance investigation.
There is no relocation pay, and the job is not remote. Commuting from Manassas to DC is manageable, with telework eligibility as a plus.
